name: Ramp
summary: Ramp provides corporate cards and finance-operations software for spend, payables, travel, and procurement.
overview: Ramp combines payments, expense management, accounts payable, procurement, and automation into a finance-operations platform.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Announced June 2026 at a $44B post-money valuation.

bull_case: Ramp can turn finance automation into a durable operating system for the CFO, expanding beyond corporate cards.
bear_case: A premium valuation, competition, and reliance on payments economics leave little room for execution mistakes.
directory_notes: $1B+ annualized revenue and positive free cash flow, per company announcement
AI agents, enterprise adoption, and payments economics.

intelligence.description: Ramp sells a finance-operations platform that combines corporate cards, expense management, bill payment, procurement, travel, and automation. The strategic question is whether the platform becomes an embedded workflow system rather than a bundle of spend tools.
company: Ramp began with corporate cards and spend controls, then expanded into bill pay, procurement, travel, accounting integrations, and AI-assisted finance workflows. Its pitch is a unified system that gives finance teams more control over each dollar and less manual work around it.

The June 2026 Series F followed a fast step-up in private-market valuation. Ramp said the capital would support further investment in AI-powered financial operations, while its disclosed annualized revenue and free-cash-flow status make it one of the more mature software-led fintechs in the private market.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Ramp is a useful read-through on whether the next generation of fintech winners capture a broad finance workflow or remain dependent on interchange and card spend. It competes for budgets with legacy expense tools, payments companies, ERPs, and newer AI finance products.

changed.text: Continued moving beyond cards into expense management, accounts payable, and procurement.
Raised new capital as the company expanded its finance-software product surface.
Announced a $750M Series F at a $44B valuation and said annualized revenue had exceeded $1B.

takeaways: Ramp's real opportunity is the finance operating system, not simply the corporate card.
The $44B valuation assumes automation can expand revenue per customer while keeping payments economics attractive.
Reported positive free cash flow distinguishes Ramp from many high-valuation private software companies.
Competition from incumbents, payments platforms, and AI-native workflow tools is the core commercial risk.
